During a focus session, Wait a Second checks supported YouTube and Instagram screens for distractions. If you opt into short-video tracking, it also detects Reels and Shorts outside sessions and saves viewer totals locally. It does not read Instagram message text or save video titles. You can turn off tracking in Statistics or disable the service in Android settings.

Viewer time includes time in a detected viewer, even when playback is paused. Detected transitions include forward and backward page changes that the app reports. They may miss swipes and do not represent unique videos.
Android applies grayscale to the whole display. You control when it starts and ends, including during a focus session.

In Android Accessibility, look for Color and motion → Color correction → Grayscale. Note your current settings before changing them. If available, add the Color correction shortcut for quick switching while using Instagram or YouTube. Turn it off or restore your previous correction mode when you finish. Names and availability vary by device.
Android handles call and message exceptions through Do Not Disturb. This list is stored on this device and gives you shortcuts to the contacts you choose.

Add a contact, open their card, and star them in Contacts. In Android Do Not Disturb or Modes, allow calls from starred contacts. If your device offers it, you can also allow messages from starred contacts. Turn on Do Not Disturb when you want these rules to apply. Other Android favorites also qualify, and WhatsApp follows its normal Android notification settings.
